title: Stooq class-share ticker fix — further non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #53 (data-provider-stooq-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: _to_stooq_symbol (backend/app/data/stooq_provider.py) checks `symbol.endswith('.us')` and returns early before the new dot-to-hyphen class-share conversion runs. A ticker that carries both a class-share dot and an explicit '.us' suffix (e.g. 'BRK.B.US') is therefore passed through as the invalid 'brk.b.us' instead of the correct 'brk-b.us' -- the exact failure mode this PR's fix eliminated for bare 'BRK.B' resurfaces for that combined input. Confirmed directly: `StooqProvider._to_stooq_symbol('BRK.B.US')` -> `'brk.b.us'`. Not introduced by this PR (the old any-dot-means-passthrough rule produced the identical wrong result), and no test covers the combined case -- only bare 'BRK.B' and bare 'aapl.us' are tested separately. Surfaced by the code-review skill during pr-reviewer's review of PR #53.

_to_stooq_symbol's narrowing of the passthrough case to *only* a trailing '.us' means an already-correctly-suffixed non-US ticker (e.g. 'SAP.DE', if Stooq's convention for it is a plain dot suffix like the old code assumed) now gets mangled: `StooqProvider._to_stooq_symbol('SAP.DE')` -> `'sap-de.us'` instead of being passed through unchanged. This is a real behavior change introduced by this PR (the old any-dot-means-passthrough rule would have left 'sap.de' alone). Low real-world impact since this app's data providers are documented/decided (data-provider-stooq-followups's own decisions entry) as targeting US equities only and no test or code path elsewhere exercises a non-US market suffix, but worth a test/doc note -- or a scoped guard if non-US suffix support is ever added -- next time this file is touched, so the tradeoff stays visible rather than only living in a decisions-array rationale.

decisions.decision: Fixed the combined-suffix case by stripping a trailing '.us' (instead of returning early on it) before the dot-to-hyphen class-share conversion runs, so 'BRK.B.US' -> 'brk-b.us'. Left the non-US-suffix case ('SAP.DE' -> 'sap-de.us', not passed through unchanged) as-is, and instead documented it explicitly in `_to_stooq_symbol`'s docstring plus a dedicated regression test (test_non_us_market_suffix_is_not_recognized_as_pre_qualified) asserting the current, intentional behavior.
decisions.rationale: The combined-suffix bug is a genuine correctness fix with no tradeoff: stripping '.us' first and re-appending it after hyphenation is strictly more correct than the early-return and doesn't change any existing passthrough behavior (aapl.us, brk-b.us both still round-trip unchanged). The non-US-suffix case is different: there's no reliable way to distinguish a genuine non-US market suffix (e.g. '.DE', '.L', '.TO' -- one or two letters, just like a single-letter class-share dot such as 'BRK.B') from class-share notation without a country-code allowlist. data-provider-stooq-followups's own decisions entry already considered and rejected exactly that allowlist as unnecessary complexity, since this provider is documented (docs/Analyse.md §9) as US-equity-only -- callers are only ever expected to pass US tickers, so 'SAP.DE' is out-of-contract input rather than a case this provider needs to handle correctly. Adding a heuristic guard now would either reintroduce the allowlist that was already rejected, or use a fragile letter-count heuristic that risks misclassifying a real class-share ticker. Chose the checklist's own offered alternative (test/doc note) over a guard for that reason.
decisions.alternatives_considered: Considered a scoped guard that raises an error for tickers ending in a plausible non-US country-code suffix, but rejected it: distinguishing 'SAP.DE' (country suffix) from 'BRK.B' (class share) by shape alone (both are TICKER.[A-Z]{1,2}) isn't reliable, and the only robust way to do it -- a country-code allowlist -- was already considered and explicitly rejected in data-provider-stooq-followups's decisions entry for this exact ambiguity.
